From 85b80fdffa867d75dfb9084a839e7949e29064e8 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Abdul Halim, Mohd Syazwan" <mohd.syazwan.abdul.halim@intel.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Nov 2023 11:26:06 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] iommu/vt-d: Add MTL to quirk list to skip TE disabling

The VT-d spec requires (10.4.4 Global Command Register, TE field) that:

Hardware implementations supporting DMA draining must drain any in-flight
DMA read/write requests queued within the Root-Complex before switching
address translation on or off and reflecting the status of the command
through the TES field in the Global Status register.

Unfortunately, some integrated graphic devices fail to do so after some
kind of power state transition. As the result, the system might stuck in
iommu_disable_translation(), waiting for the completion of TE transition.

Add MTL to the quirk list for those devices and skips TE disabling if the
qurik hits.

Fixes: b1012ca8dc4f ("iommu/vt-d: Skip TE disabling on quirky gfx dedicated iommu")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Abdul Halim, Mohd Syazwan <mohd.syazwan.abdul.halim@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Lu Baolu <baolu.lu@linux.intel.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20231116022324.30120-1-baolu.lu@linux.intel.com
Signed-off-by: Joerg Roedel <jroedel@suse.de>

diff --git a/drivers/iommu/intel/iommu.c b/drivers/iommu/intel/iommu.c
index 4c257ccf9dc3..68f121c28fbf 100644
--- a/drivers/iommu/intel/iommu.c
+++ b/drivers/iommu/intel/iommu.c
@@ -5077,7 +5077,7 @@ static void quirk_igfx_skip_te_disable(struct pci_dev *dev)
 	ver = (dev->device >> 8) & 0xff;
 	if (ver != 0x45 && ver != 0x46 && ver != 0x4c &&
 	    ver != 0x4e && ver != 0x8a && ver != 0x98 &&
-	    ver != 0x9a && ver != 0xa7)
+	    ver != 0x9a && ver != 0xa7 && ver != 0x7d)
 		return;
 
 	if (risky_device(dev))
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/iommu/intel/iommu.c`**
   - A new version check was added to the `quirk_igfx_skip_te_disable` function. Specifically, the condition now includes an additional check for the version `0x7d`. This means that if the device version is `0x7d`, the function will now also skip the TE (Translation Enable) disabling process, in addition to the previously listed versions.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in the `iommu.c` file is aimed at addressing a specific issue related to integrated graphic devices that fail to properly handle DMA requests after power state transitions. By adding the version `0x7d` to the quirk list, the patch ensures that devices with this version will also benefit from the same TE disabling skip that was previously applied to other versions. This change is part of a broader effort to enhance system stability and prevent the system from getting stuck in the `iommu_disable_translation()` function due to these quirks in hardware behavior.

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from certain integrated graphic devices failing to drain in-flight DMA read/write requests after a power state transition, which leads to the system getting stuck in the `iommu_disable_translation()` function while waiting for the TE (Translation Enable) transition to complete. This behavior violates the VT-d specification requirements for handling DMA draining during address translation changes.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void quirk_igfx_skip_te_disable(struct pci_dev *dev)
 {
 	unsigned short ver;
 
 	if (!IS_GFX_DEVICE(dev))
 		return;
 
 	ver = (dev->device >> 8) & 0xff;
 	if (ver != 0x45 && ver != 0x46 && ver != 0x4c &&
 	    ver != 0x4e && ver != 0x8a && ver != 0x98 &&
-	    ver != 0x9a && ver != 0xa7)
+	    ver != 0x9a && ver != 0xa7 && ver != 0x7d)
 		return;
 
 	if (risky_device(dev))
 		return;
 
 	pci_info(dev, "Skip IOMMU disabling for graphics\n");
 	iommu_skip_te_disable = 1;
 }
 DECLARE_PCI_FIXUP_HEADER(PCI_VENDOR_ID_INTEL, PCI_ANY_ID, quirk_igfx_skip_te_disable);

This conditional statement checks the version of the integrated graphics device. If the version does not match any of the specified values, the function returns without applying any quirks. This can lead to the system getting stuck in `iommu_disable_translation()` for certain devices that fail to drain in-flight DMA requests after a power state transition, violating the VT-d specification.

The code statements that fix the bug are:

